instruction: Focused review supporting the proposed when-to-think and what-to-think experiments.
scope: Causal private preparation during multi-party meeting speech, with separate timing and work-content controls
sub_questions: When should a useful speech update activate private reasoning?
What should preparation retain or derive before a future question is known?
How do speaker attribution, decision revisions and uncertainty affect usefulness?
How can computation cost, readiness and useful spoken latency be compared fairly?

papers.title: LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning
papers.problem: A speech pipeline must decide when a prefix is useful enough to process.
papers.method: A lightweight semantic trigger activates reasoning; separate background state maintenance and foreground response work are coordinated asynchronously.
papers.results: Reports improved accuracy/latency/efficiency trade-offs on its spoken-task benchmarks.
papers.relevance: Compare meaningful information changes with fixed time intervals. This work already studies when-to-think and structured state; those ideas alone are not a novelty claim.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: Don’t Wait to Reply: Towards Responsive yet Thoughtful Dialogue through Proactive Thinking
papers.problem: Waiting for a new user turn before reasoning adds latency.
papers.method: Anticipate possible replies, prepare responses, then verify which prepared reasoning can be reused when the actual reply arrives.
papers.results: Reports latency benefits in time-aware simulated dialogue tasks.
papers.relevance: A speculative-question baseline is relevant, but predicted questions must never be replaced by the actual held-out question. Charge failed predictions too.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: DuplexOmni: Real-Time Listening, Seeing, Thinking, and Speaking for Full-Duplex Interaction
papers.problem: Continuous interaction and slower reasoning need to cooperate.
papers.method: A streaming interaction layer requests asynchronous reasoning/tool assistance and consumes returned guidance.
papers.results: Reports full-duplex interaction results; our local reproductions establish only selected cases.
papers.relevance: Reuse the existing S1/S2 handoff. An external background controller is an experimental policy, not evidence that native S1 learned when to prepare.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: Agents Thinking Fast and Slow: A Talker-Reasoner Architecture
papers.authors: Konstantina Christakopoulou, Shibl Mourad and Maja Matarić
papers.problem: Conversing and longer planning require different response speeds.
papers.method: A fast conversational component uses state produced by a slower reasoning/planning component.
papers.results: Provides a sleep-coaching case study and qualitative discussion.
papers.relevance: Use explicit state as the interface between private work and outward speech. Keep whether-to-speak separate from whether-to-prepare.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: Thinking While Speaking: Inference-Time Knowledge Transfer for Responsive and Intelligent Conversational Voice Agents
papers.problem: Immediate conversation and slow external reasoning have different latency needs.
papers.method: Conversational infill lets a small talker begin grounded speech and incorporate streamed reasoning results.
papers.results: Reports trained infill models, benchmark evaluations and a user study; the checked version is v3, July 2026.
papers.relevance: Measure the first correct useful fact, not only the first acknowledgement or filler. Infill training is separate from our present controller study.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
papers.problem: Long histories challenge extraction, updates, time reasoning and calibrated uncertainty.
papers.method: A benchmark and indexing/retrieval/reading framework distinguish memory storage from finding and using it.
papers.results: ICLR 2025 paper; reports benefits from fact granularity, time-aware retrieval and structured reading.
papers.relevance: Separate omitted facts from retrieval/answer errors. Correctly reporting missing information is useful, but is not proof that older facts were recalled.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: GroupMemBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent Memory in Multi-Party Conversations
papers.problem: Group memory must retain who believes or undertook what, not just a bag of facts.
papers.method: Graph-grounded synthetic group conversations and asker-specific queries test updates, ambiguity, temporal and multi-step reasoning.
papers.results: Finds strong memory systems still lose important group structure; results concern synthetic text conversations.
papers.relevance: Speaker labels are a perception/input aid. The preparation task must still distinguish the person speaking, the person responsible and the current decision state.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
papers.authors: Charlie Snell, Jaehoon Lee, Kelvin Xu and Aviral Kumar
papers.problem: The same inference budget need not suit every problem.
papers.method: Study adaptive allocation between search/verifiers and iterative response revision on known prompts.
papers.results: Reports prompt-dependent compute-efficiency gains; this is not a streaming meeting experiment.
papers.relevance: Compare quality and delay at measured cost. A token cap is only a budget limit, not proof of equal GPU work, and future question difficulty is unavailable before the request.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: Speculative Interaction Agents: Building Real-Time Agents with Asynchronous I/O and Speculative Tool Calling
papers.problem: New user or tool information can arrive while work is pending.
papers.method: Asynchronous input/output and revisable speculative tool calls let processing overlap external waits.
papers.results: Reports speed-ups on tool-calling benchmarks; tools and their execution risk differ from private note preparation.
papers.relevance: Include cancellation and revision. A private preparation trigger must not automatically authorize an outward response or a tool action.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

papers.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
papers.problem: Repeatedly reading full conversation history is costly.
papers.method: Extract, consolidate and retrieve salient facts, with an additional graph-memory variant.
papers.results: Reports memory/latency/token-cost comparisons on LOCOMO; these are not causal multi-speaker audio measurements.
papers.relevance: Use a compact fact ledger as a baseline, then test whether retaining owner, uncertainty and revisions adds value over a plain summary.
papers.verification: Primary arXiv abstract and, for the central methods, full HTML checked 2026-10-27

themes: Background preparation and asynchronous speech/reasoning have close prior work.
Memory quality depends on storage, retrieval and correct use; compactness alone is not enough.
Input attribution and preparation objectives are separate design choices.
The latency to a useful fact and the cost of all unused preparation matter alongside response onset.

gaps.statement: A practical target is controlled evaluation of preparation timing and content under speaker/ASR mistakes and changed decisions, rather than claiming that asynchronous reasoning itself is new.
Keep actual future questions out of preparation and measure the complete workload, including prefill, discarded updates and gating.
